ordered_diagnoses: Sister Mary Joseph nodule due to transverse colon cancer

facts.raw_span: A 55-year-old man with no significant medical history
presented with a 10-month history of spontaneous, progressively painful umbilical discomfort
a firm nodule at the umbilicus that gradually increased in size and became ulcerated and tender
The umbilical lesion measured 6 cm by 6 cm, was ulcerated over its entire surface, and bled on contact
Deep palpation of the abdomen revealed a poorly defined, firm mass approximately 8 cm in diameter in the right hypochondrium
Biopsy of the umbilical lesion demonstrated a well-differentiated, infiltrating adenocarcinoma
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT showed homogeneously enhancing umbilical tissue growth
irregular, circumferential thickening of the right third of the transverse colon measuring approximately 8.3 cm
Total colonoscopy revealed no endoluminal lesion

concepts.preferred_label: Sister Mary Joseph nodule due to transverse colon cancer
concepts.why: The patient's umbilical lesion is consistent with a Sister Mary Joseph nodule, which is a metastasis from an intra-abdominal malignancy, in this case, likely from the transverse colon cancer.

The biopsy of the umbilical lesion demonstrated a well-differentiated, infiltrating adenocarcinoma, and the CT scan showed irregular, circumferential thickening of the right third of the transverse colon, consistent with colon cancer.
